native.context.syntax.v2.note: The native context of the syntax-only mode. It carries exactly what interprets a body span when there is no compiler: the retained, closure-bound GRAMMAR BUNDLE and the normalizer specification it uses. It deliberately has no toolchain, no stdlib, no lockfile, no node_modules layout and no config graph, because a grammar-only analysis reads none of them; a syntax-only context that named a compiler would be claiming semantics it never computed.

dialect.selectionLaw: TypeScript has no per-crate dialect map; its per-body axis is the SOURCE VARIANT its own file suffix denotes, which decides how the body is scanned and parsed. Longest matching suffix wins, so .d.ts is never read as .ts. An unlisted suffix REFUSES rather than being folded into a neighbouring variant, so a normal variant is never silently mis-assigned and a new one must be registered deliberately. Distinct suffixes stay distinct even where a parser would treat two alike: this can fail to equate two bodies that are in fact equivalent, and can never equate two the language reads differently. Collapsing variants is a claim about a parser and belongs to the level specification. Only the variant token enters the record; the path does not.

excluded.libSelection: standard library selection resolves types; it does not interpret a body span
excluded.typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot: same, and it is a retained artifact digest not a language identity
excluded.languageMode: configuration and program assembly, not the language
excluded.synthesizerVersion: the option synthesizer, not the compiler that reads the body
excluded.packageModuleType: module resolution semantics, not body interpretation
excluded.anchorPath: the path establishes the variant and then does not enter the record; two identical bodies at different paths in one variant have one identity

languageVersionBinding.bodyLanguageLaw: The body languageId is DERIVED from the selected source variant, not from the provider universe. The universe language is the engine that reads the body; a .js body read by the TypeScript engine is a javascript body and must carry that identifier, exactly as native section 6.3 requires. The frame languageId and the record languageId are both taken from this one selector over the same anchor, so they cannot disagree. No JavaScript body is rewritten as TypeScript, and the cross-tsjs candidate projection of section 6.4 is untouched.

dialect.selectionLaw: The dialect is the EFFECTIVE edition of the SELECTED compilation target that owns this body path: the unit targetEdition when it states one, otherwise the universe edition map entry for its crateName. There is NO fast path - Cargo lets a target override its package default, so package defaults that all agree still do not determine a body dialect - and a clones fact over any Rust universe therefore requires the committed SourceUnitOwnershipV1 whatever the package map looks like. The order of decision is fixed and each step has its own cause: (1) no committed ownership refuses; (2) enumeration partial refuses BEFORE any row is looked at, so incomplete discovery can never act as an implicit edition selection by hiding a conflicting owner; (3) rows are those whose path EQUALS the enclosing fact anchor path - never a prefix, never a nearest directory, never a first match - and no row at all refuses as not-compiled; (4) rows are then restricted to selectedUnitIds, and a path compiled only by unselected targets refuses as not-selected rather than borrowing an out-of-scope edition; (5) SELECTED owners whose effective editions AGREE are admissible, which is the ordinary shared-file and lib-plus-test-target case; (6) selected owners that DISAGREE are an ambiguous unselected request and refuse. Because selectedUnitIds is committed inside the record whose H identity the universe names, each selection is a DIFFERENT sourceUniverse: one physical path compiled at two editions is validly analysed under each, one selection at a time. Selection establishes the JOIN only - no path, crate name, unit id or selection enters the body-language-version record.
dialect.scopeVersusEnumeration: SELECTED SCOPE and INCOMPLETE ENUMERATION are different claims and neither substitutes for the other. A selection says these targets ARE the analysis, so an owner outside them is deliberately out of scope and its edition does not bear on this body; the selection is committed in the identity, so it is visible to every consumer and changes the universe. Incomplete enumeration says the producer did not finish, so an owner INSIDE the selected scope may exist that is not listed and could contradict a listed one; that is a gap in knowledge, it is not visible as a selection, and it therefore admits no body dialect at all. Silently omitting a conflicting owner from the units table is not a selection either: an omission leaves no trace, whereas a selection is part of the universe identity. Partial evidence stays useful under the existing law rather than voiding a Run: the clones scope simply mints no body identity, its Coverage carries the incompleteness, the predicate is indeterminate and the seal is indeterminate.

excluded.sysrootDigest: retained artifact of the resolution environment, not a language identity
excluded.rustcDevLlvmDigest: code generation backend; it does not interpret a body span
excluded.cargoVersion: build and dependency tool; it does not read the body
excluded.crateRootPaths: paths, and a body identity must not vary with where a crate sits

languageVersionBinding.dialectRepresentableForm: An ordinary mixed-edition workspace has a representable valid form: each source path is owned by units of one edition, so every body gets its own dialect and bodies of BOTH editions close in the same universe. Only a path genuinely compiled under two different editions refuses.

native.semantic-universe.syntax.v2.note: The universe of the syntax-only mode. `semantic universe` names the thing that DETERMINES a fact, and for a grammar-only analysis that is the selected bundled-grammar set, not a compiler semantic model. It exists because the capability matrix advertises declares/literal/control-flow at `syntactic` and clones at `normalized-body-hash` for syntax-only, and because file/package/vcs-change inventory facts must be representable in a repository that contains no TypeScript and no Rust unit at all: fact2 and subject-scope both REQUIRE a universe h-identity from this closed domain set, so with only the two compiler universes registered those advertised cells could mint no fact and no scope. Making the universe fields nullable was rejected: it would delete the invariant that every fact states what produced it, and would leave `which grammar read this body` unanswerable for exactly the facts that depend on it. Semantic capability is NOT widened by this domain - a syntax-only universe can carry only the syntactic and inventory rungs and the clones rung; imports/references/calls/types/reachability remain language-tier-unsupported, and a universal negative still requires its own complete Coverage.

languageVersionBinding.componentLaw: body-language-version names THE COMPONENT THAT INTERPRETS THE BODY SPAN - explicitly not the build tool and not the resolver. Under syntax-only that component is the bundled grammar's parser, so the three fields are bound to the retained, closure-joined grammar bundle rather than to a toolchain. No static constant and no fabricated compiler identity is used: parserVersion is joined by admission to the grammar closure's manifest semanticVersion exactly as the compiler versions are, and bundleDigest is the exact retained bundle identity. A body read by the grammar therefore has a DIFFERENT languageVersion from the same bytes read by tsc or rustc, so their clone identities differ. That is required, not incidental: equating a grammar parse with a compiler parse would assert an interpretation that was never performed.

dialect.selectionLaw: A syntax-only analysis has no compilation unit, so it has no edition to select and no program to join; its only per-body axis is the variant the bundled grammar selects from the body's own suffix. Longest matching suffix wins, so .d.ts is never read as .ts. A suffix with no bundled grammar REFUSES rather than being folded into a neighbouring variant - which is the same conservative rule the compiler universes use, and it is what keeps `unsupported-file / no-bundled-grammar` an honest classification rather than a silent reinterpretation. Crucially there is NO edition branch here: a .rs body read without Cargo has no admitted ownership, and inventing one would be exactly the fabricated compiler semantics this mode exists to avoid.

It previously mapped to null, and because fact2/subject-scope require a universe h-identity from a closed set of two compiler domains, the syntax and clones cells the capability matrix advertises for that mode - and every file/package/vcs-change fact in a repository with no TypeScript or Rust unit - could mint no fact and no scope.

closureKinds.standing: Which closure kind each closure-bearing field admits. Stated so no field is left to guess.
closureKinds.note: No new closure kind is invented for producer acts: enumeration, view production, fact production and stage production are all provider acts under the existing kind. `grammar` is a genuinely new INSTALLED-COMPONENT kind, in the same family as `toolchain`, `stdlib` and `rust-dev-llvm`: the syntax-only mode's body interpreter is a bundled grammar set, and binding it to an existing kind would either claim it is a toolchain (it executes no compiler) or leave the component that interprets a body span outside the closure law, which is the one thing every other universe pins down.

scopeCapabilityLaw.standing: Normative, and consumed by BOTH the native producer admission boundary and identity Run closure. It states what a COVERAGE claim over a body-dialect relation means under a universe whose dialect form is a closed suffix table. The per-BODY selector (`dialect.onUnknown`) was already total, but it is only reached while a body is being derived, so a scope that produced NO fact was classified by nothing and could claim a determinate `complete` for a path the universe cannot read in any dialect. Coverage is a claim about the EXAMINATION and must not be decided by whether the examination happened to produce output.
scopeCapabilityLaw.gate: Relations carrying a `bodyIdentityJoin` in the relation registry, which is where the dialect axis is consulted at all. Nothing here claims a suffix table decides SYMBOL capability, and no compiler, parser or grammar is executed, ranked or qualified: the only question asked is whether the path's own suffix selects a variant in the table this universe published.
scopeCapabilityLaw.subjectLaw: The relation registry's own `subjectKind`. A `source-path` relation is judged on ALL of THIS scope's subjects, so a mixed scope cannot hide its unsupported part behind its supported one. Any other subject kind is judged on the committed snapshot inventory, where at least one path must be readable, because the retained record associates an opaque subject id with no path.
scopeCapabilityLaw.emptySubjects: Unsupported. An empty `source-path` scope is never vacuously supported.
scopeCapabilityLaw.inventoryExempt: `file@enumerated`, `package@manifest-declared` and `vcs-change@vcs-reported` are never dialect-gated. A snapshot inventories every file it contains, so inventory evidence keeps its promised meaning on every inventoried path including ones no dialect reads.
scopeCapabilityLaw.onSupportedScope: Eligible for `complete` even when the scope contains no body at all. An absent body is a finding; an absent capability is not.
scopeCapabilityLaw.notAProofOfAbsence: An unsupported scope is NOT a finding that no such construct exists. It is the disclosure that this universe never had the capability to look, which is the same principle the syntax universe's grammar-capability law already encodes.
scopeCapabilityLaw.distinctFromOwnerNotCompiled: Deliberately NOT the treatment `BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_NOT_COMPILED` gets. That refusal describes a path which IS a source file of the universe's language and which no selected compilation target owns - the universe examined it and produced a resolution fact about a known language, so `complete` stays lawful there. A suffix outside the table is not a body of this universe in ANY dialect, so there is nothing it could have examined and a determinate answer would assert a negative from an absent capability.
scopeCapabilityLaw.refusals: A false `complete`, a wrong deficiency and a wrong or null cause each refuse separately and by their own name: `native.coverage-source-variant-*` at the producer boundary and `COVERAGE_SOURCE_VARIANT_*` at retained Run closure. Both name sets are retained and distinct, but they are NOT both reachable for every scope: where the producer boundary can already apply this law it refuses first, so the closure name is not reached for that case. Which name a scenario yields is decided by which boundary sees the defect first, not by a precedence among the names.
scopeCapabilityLaw.guardOrder: TWO boundaries decide this, in this order. FIRST the native Coverage PRODUCER admission, which judges ONE record and never sees the snapshot, so it applies this law only where the scope carries its own paths - a `source-path` relation with a `bodyIdentityJoin` - and only when its caller supplies the owning universe's dialect, as Run closure does. A FALSE `complete` for a path whose suffix no dialect table lists is refused THERE, before any Run-closure prerequisite runs. THEN, at Run closure, the prerequisites in their own order: the compilation-ownership axis, then the syntax grammar-capability registry, then this law as the backstop that makes the set of published universes total. Each keeps its own refusal name for the cases it is the first to decide; for the syntax universe this law is a strictly weaker necessary condition its own registry already implies, because that registry publishes that no data-document suffix appears in the syntax dialect table. An HONESTLY DISCLOSED unsupported scope is ADMITTED at both boundaries and closes its Run carrying `onUnsupportedScope`; only a false or mismatched claim refuses.

value.languageVersionBindingLaw: Normative, and consumed by identity Run closure. The languageVersion component of a FACT-IDENTITY body frame is the RAW 32 BYTES of SHA-256(C(body-language-version)) - the same fixed-width treatment the inherited grammar already gives levelVersion, so the inherited frame bytes and field grammar are unchanged and the component is bounded for every valid input. Fixed width is not a convenience: the inherited frame gives each component a u8 length, and a component that embedded per-crate or per-package data is not representable for ordinary valid inputs. The record is DERIVED: closure rebuilds it from the universe ResolvedInputs, the admitted retained native context the universe own nativeContextId names, the enclosing fact own anchor and the retained nested records the universe commits, and compares. It carries the identity of the component that INTERPRETS the body span plus the SELECTED source dialect, and nothing else: not operational platform, not paths, not names, not resolution inputs, not build tooling, not option synthesis, and no per-crate or per-package collection. Every language declares its dialect axis explicitly; there is no null branch and no unexamined default. A universe domain used by a clones fact with no binding refuses, and every dialect branch that cannot SELECT refuses with a distinct cause rather than guessing.

parameter.note: An analysis-spec or stage-spec parameter may only cite a document on this closed list. That replaces the withdrawn "a payload schema document must constrain the payload directly" rule, which contradicted the native and workflow bundle registries. A cited schema with no row refuses: there is no default row, no caller-selected schema and no permissive fallback for an unregistered parameter.

selectionCardinality.law: ONE Plan selects AT MOST ONE parameter per registered row. Zero is legal for a row this analysis does not need; two or more entries of analysis-spec.parameters (or stage-spec.parameters) whose schemaDigest resolves to the SAME row are REFUSED, whatever their payloadDigests are. This is a SELECTION rule about how many entries a SPEC may carry and is a different question from keyIsTheDocumentNotThePair, which is about how many REGISTRY ROWS one document digest may resolve to; PAYLOAD_PARAMETER_AMBIGUOUS_ROW answers the second and never constrained the first.
selectionCardinality.why: A parameter row is a Plan INPUT: the payload it cites is the value the analysis is run with. Two entries under one row put two different values in one input slot and nothing decides which is the Plan's. Both enter analysisSpecDigest and therefore PlanId, so two conforming hosts could bind different documents from ONE admitted Plan and the resulting comparison axis would attribute differently for the same PlanId. Refusing is the registry declining an arbitrary selection, exactly as it does for an ambiguous row. There is deliberately NO default, NO first-listed or last-listed winner, and NO merge.
selectionCardinality.zeroIsLegal: An ordinary analysis that does not need a scope-policy input selects no ScopeDocumentV1 parameter and closes. A caller that DOES need it - baseline adoption and comparison - still gets the explicit missing-selection refusal from the workflow binding verifier; absence is never silently substituted, and the foundation scope-descriptor named by plan.scopeDigest is a DIFFERENT record that never stands in for ScopeDocumentV1.
selectionCardinality.exactDuplicatesAreADifferentRefusal: Two BYTE-IDENTICAL parameter entries are a malformed record, not an ambiguous selection: analysis-spec.parameters is uniqueItems with x-opensip-order canonical-set, so a whole-item duplicate refuses on the schema and on the collection order law (ORDER_OR_DUPLICATE) before any selection question is asked. This rule owns only the case those cannot see: DISTINCT entries citing one row.
enforcedAt: the PRE-PLAN analysis-spec admission boundary (native_evidence_model.admit_analysis_spec, after schema and vocabulary admission)
retained Run closure over the retained analysis-spec (identity-model close_run, ANALYSIS_SPEC_PARAMETER_SELECTION_AMBIGUOUS)
independently in the bounded workflow scope binding verifier when it is called directly (workflows_model.verify_scope_parameter_binding)
selectionCardinality.precedence: MOST SPECIFIC FIRST. The import-source-context row keeps its own named guard IMPORT_SOURCE_CONTEXT_MULTIPLE where that guard runs - inside the Run-closure import derivation, which is the boundary that consumes the row - and this generic selection guard is the TOTAL backstop that runs for every row and every Plan, including one with no selected import. Nothing about the import row's zero/one/multiple rule changes: zero means an empty declared-build set, one is the selection, more than one is refused.
selectionCardinality.notAStageSpecDuplicate: A stage-spec carries a SUBSET of the Plan analysis-spec parameters (STAGE_SPEC_HIDDEN_PARAMETER), so a Plan admitted under this rule cannot contain a stage that selects a row twice; the stage-spec case is implied rather than separately guarded, and stating that is not a claim that a second guard exists.

parameter.keyIsTheDocumentNotThePair: Normative accounting of a bounded limitation, retained deliberately (CB4-ADV-4). The key is the cited schemaDigest, which is the SHA-256 of the whole DOCUMENT's bytes, not a (document, selector) pair. Both rows are distinguishable today - import-source-context.schema.json and policy-document.schema.json are different documents with different digests - so there is no ambiguity in this release. The limitation is structural and is stated rather than left to be rediscovered: a SECOND parameter row selecting another $def out of a document an existing row already cites would be indistinguishable by this key, and the first listed would otherwise silently win. That case is FORBIDDEN and refuses (PAYLOAD_PARAMETER_AMBIGUOUS_ROW), which is the registry law declining to make an arbitrary selection rather than a defect. Note that the same policy-document.schema.json bytes are also named by plan.policyDigest and plan.waiverDigest, but under the `canonical-record` representation and a different payload CLASS, so those are not in this key space and raise no collision.
parameter.whyNotRekeyByDocumentAndSelector: Re-keying the class by (document, selector) would lift the restriction and would change no identity today, and it is deliberately NOT done here. No existing requirement needs a second $def out of one document as a parameter; adding flexibility no requirement asks for would widen the closed key space and the admission surface for a case that does not exist, and would retire an explicit refusal in exchange for a rule that has never been exercised. If such a requirement ever arises it is an explicit versioned design correction with its own controls - not a silent widening, and not something an implementer may assume.

value.standing: Selected evaluator3 contract; source acceptance and product qualification are recorded separately.
value.majorLaw: Changed output domains dispatch explicitly to version3 records and prefixes. Frozen version2 bytes remain historical; no coercion or permissive mixed-version parse. Unchanged ancestors referenced by digest retain their existing identifier majors; their values change if committed input/schema bytes change.
value.integrationStatus: Public identity-model.v3.close_run performs owner/native/schema admission and complete evaluator replay, including retained execution-input totality. Workflow and security adapters consume this boundary. Synthetic reference graphs do not qualify a compiler, host, platform or release.

value.standing: Normative and CLOSED. For every DeficiencyV2 member, WHICH retained field carries its cause and what that field must say. There is no default row: a deficiency with no row here is a registry defect and refuses. Nothing in this registry changes DeficiencyV2, NativeCause, UnresolvedEdgeKindV1, ClosedWorldV2, the public DomainDetailCode registry or any D9 class, code or exit; every carrier it names already exists and is already closed.
value.whyItIsNeeded: native-evidence section 10 labels its second column `Cause (nativeCause)` and then fills three of its rows with values that are not NativeCause members: `the unresolved edge classes; partial/not-attempted stage` for `resolution-incomplete`, `exports-open, exports-unknown` for `external-consumers-unknown`, and `compiler-inferred present` for `derivation-policy-unmet`. Each refuses schema validation as a nativeCause (`'computed-member-access' is not valid under any of the given schemas`), so the only representable value was null - which the NativeCause description itself defines as `a disclosure was owed and not made`. Worse, nothing compared the pair to anything: on the frozen reference a `resolution-incomplete` entry carrying the unrelated but schema-valid `lockfile-missing`, or relabelled `capability-missing`, or a `derivation-policy-unmet` with an empty derivationKinds, or an `external-consumers-unknown` over `exportsClosed: closed`, each closed a Run. A cause vocabulary that nothing derives and nothing compares leaves the disclosure optional in practice - the same argument that added the three body-language-* members, carried through to the rest of the table.
value.whyNotMoreEnumMembers: Adding NativeCause members was rejected on the merits, not for compatibility. `resolution-incomplete` has a genuinely SET-VALUED cause: an entry can exhibit up to all sixteen UnresolvedEdgeKindV1 classes at once, and a scalar cannot carry them, so enum members would either lose information or force an arbitrary pick - the multi-cause defect the finding names. All three rows already have closed, structured, independently DERIVED carriers in the same record: unresolvedEdgeClasses (which RC-2 already forces to equal the admitted unresolved-edge facts), ClosedWorldV2.exportsClosed, and derivationKinds. The correction is to NAME those carriers and ENFORCE the join, not to duplicate them in a scalar.
value.nullIsNotAnEscape: Where a row says nativeCause MUST be null, that null no longer records an unmade disclosure: the row names the field that carries the cause instead, and admission REFUSES unless that field actually carries it. A `resolution-incomplete` entry whose resolutionCompleteness claims `complete` is refused, so `null` cannot be used to say nothing.
value.multiCauseAndPrecedence: An entry carries ONE deficiency and simultaneously carries every carrier this registry names. What each carrier RETAINS differs, and an earlier revision wrongly generalised the strongest case to all of them by saying the scalar `loses nothing`. The accurate statement is per carrier: resolutionCompleteness.unresolvedEdgeClasses is a genuine SET and retains EVERY applicable unresolved class at once, already forced by RC-2 to equal the admitted unresolved-edge facts of the view; closedWorld and derivationKinds are independent fields that retain their own state whatever the deficiency is; but input-closure-incomplete's carrier is a SINGLE SCALAR NativeCause, and a Run can genuinely be missing several inputs at once - two absent crates, or an absent crate AND an unavailable generated file. For that row the retained cause is a SELECTED one, not the full set. See selectedScalarCauseLimitation. Which single deficiency is declared when several apply is the section 10 precedence order, applied by the owning sufficiency evaluation against a REQUIREMENT. That selection is deliberately NOT re-derived from the entry alone, and the limit is stated rather than worked around: several conditions are requirement-relative (external-consumer state matters only for a universal negative about an exported target; the confidence floor lives in the Requirement, not the entry), and RC-3 makes `coverage: complete` with `state: incomplete` and NO deficiency a valid honest entry. Forcing a deficiency from exhibited entry evidence would therefore refuse lawful Runs. What IS decidable from the entry is the direction enforced here: a DECLARED deficiency must be SUPPORTED by the entry's own committed evidence.
value.retainedVersusPublicRoute: Two different routes and neither substitutes for the other. RETAINED: the whole ViewEntryV3 lives inside the coverage2 record, whose payload digest and schema digest the Run commits, so every carrier named below is retained evidence a verifier can re-derive. PUBLIC: the DEFICIENCY is projected outward as its own closed DomainDetailCode - `resolution-incomplete`, `external-consumers-unknown` and `derivation-policy-unmet` are all already members - and the CAUSE travels as typed detail in the coverage2 record the host termination names by its coverageId, exactly as section 10 has always said for the nativeCause-carried rows. No new public code is added and none is needed.

language-tier-unsupported.rule: The admitted universe's selected grammars do not bear the requested relation@rung. The cause is a single named state, so nativeCause carries it and must be exactly capability-missing. Already derived and enforced by the syntax capability prerequisite; stated here so one table covers every member.

provider-unavailable.rule: Section 10 leaves this row's Cause cell empty, so a null is lawful and self-describing; where a more specific named state applies it is carried. No other cause may appear.

input-closure-incomplete.rule: The one deficiency whose cause genuinely IS a single named missing input, which is why section 10 lists twelve of them and why the three body-language-* members were added here. A null refuses: this row is exactly where a null would record an unmade disclosure.

budget-exhausted.rule: Section 10 already qualifies this row `(stage terminal)`. The stage terminal is the cause and it is a closed StageTerminal value in the same entry, so nativeCause is null by design and the terminal must actually say budget-exhausted.

confidence-floor-unmet.rule: Requirement-relative and deliberately without an entry carrier: the FLOOR lives in RequirementV2.minConfidenceMillionths and the entry carries only its own confidenceMillionths, so the entry cannot decide whether the floor was met. The comparison is the sufficiency evaluation's, and stating that limit is honest where inventing an entry-level predicate would not be.

derivation-policy-unmet.relationLaw: The OWNING law scopes this deficiency to one relation. Native section 4.7 and sufficiency_v2 apply derivationPolicy only where `rel == "types"` and the requirement asks for `declared-only`; there is no derivation policy for any other relation, so no other relation's entry can be short of one. An earlier revision checked the derivationKinds carrier ALONE, and a complete Run therefore admitted this declared deficiency on a `references` entry that merely carried the same array value (root diagnostic: references ADMIT, types ADMIT). An entry whose relation is outside this list cannot declare it.
derivation-policy-unmet.rule: Section 10's Cause cell reads `compiler-inferred present`, which is a statement about derivationKinds - a closed three-member set in this same entry - and not a NativeCause. The entry must actually carry compiler-inferred among its derivation kinds.
derivation-policy-unmet.thisIsDeclarationSupportNotAnObligation: Two different assertions, and only the first is enforced. (1) An entry that DECLARES this deficiency must be for relation `types` and must actually carry `compiler-inferred`. (2) Whether a given requirement DEMANDS the deficiency is sufficiency_v2's question against a RequirementV2, and is not derived here. `compiler-inferred` types are exact under the admitted universe and are perfectly valid under `derivationPolicy=any`; they become a deficiency only under `declared-only`. Nothing here imposes declared-only on a valid types entry, and controls hold both directions.

resolution-incomplete.rule: Section 10's Cause cell reads `the unresolved edge classes; partial/not-attempted stage`, and both halves are ResolutionCompletenessV2 fields: `state` names the stage condition and `unresolvedEdgeClasses` carries EVERY applicable class at once, already forced by RC-2 to equal the admitted unresolved-edge facts of this view. A claim of this deficiency over a `complete` or `not-applicable` resolution state is refused: that is the entry contradicting its own evidence.

external-consumers-unknown.rule: Section 10's Cause cell reads `exports-open, exports-unknown`, which are the ClosedWorldV2 exportsClosed values `open` and `unknown` in this same entry, not NativeCause members. `closed` refuses: an entry cannot claim its consumers are unknown while its own closed-world record says they are closed.

required-relation-missing.rule: A sufficiency verdict about a relation the view does NOT carry an entry for, so an entry can never be its own evidence. It has no entry carrier by construction and takes no cause. Kept admissible rather than refused because nothing in this contract states that a host may not record it, and inventing that refusal is not this correction's to make.

value.noDeficiencyNoCause: A null deficiency requires a null nativeCause. A cause without a deficiency names why nothing went wrong, which is not a claim this record can carry.
value.enforcedAt: native_evidence_model admit_coverage_result_v3 - the producer boundary - and therefore again at identity-model.v3.open_run_closure, which re-runs that exact admission over the RETAINED coverage payload (native owner admission, not evaluator correctness). identity-model.v3.close_run is complete replay of evaluator3 output. Refusals are native.coverage-cause-* and are PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION like the other producer-boundary refusals.
value.selectedScalarCauseLimitation: STATED LIMITATION, not a defect to be engineered around. input-closure-incomplete retains ONE NativeCause while several missing inputs may coexist. Provenance of the selection: the producer names the cause it acted on, and Run closure checks that the named cause is lawful for the deficiency - it does not and cannot enumerate the inputs that were not named. What IS fully retained beside it is the rest of the Coverage entry and the Run's own evidence: the missing dependency sources, prepared rows and generated files are retained records in their own right, so a consumer that needs the complete set reads those rather than the scalar. No multi-cause format is introduced merely to make the prose true; the bounded source/ownership laws stay exactly as they are, and the limitation is published so no consumer reads the scalar as exhaustive.

perRequirementConsumerBoundary.standing: Normative and CLOSED. WHERE a per-requirement sufficiency_v2 outcome travels once it leaves this unit, and in WHICH vocabulary. This block adds no member to DeficiencyV2, changes no carrier row above, adds no D9 class, code, exit or public detail code, and changes no D9 projection: it names the consumer boundary that was previously unnamed.
perRequirementConsumerBoundary.producer: native-evidence.md section 4.6 `sufficiency_v2`, evaluated once per RequirementV2 against one NATIVE view, and therefore defined for the thirteen native fact relations only. Its FULL result is {satisfied, deficiency?, disclosures, causes}: `causes` is returned on BOTH branches - empty when satisfied - and `disclosures` may be non-empty on the FAILING branch as well. An earlier revision called the result shape closed and total as {satisfied:true,disclosures} or {satisfied:false,deficiency}; that described only the two fields a consumer projects, not the producer's output, and is corrected here.

consumers.carries: the DeficiencyV2 member sufficiency_v2 returned for THIS requirement
consumers.vocabulary: urn:opensip:product-v1:workflows:common#/$defs/NativeSufficiencyDeficiency for a NATIVE-plane requirement - a generated/drift-checked mirror of #/$defs/DeficiencyV2 in its declared member order, because the workflows bundle resolves only workflows URNs and takes no cross-bundle $ref. An IMPORTED-plane requirement of the same record carries #/$defs/ImportedRequirementDeficiency instead, under its own owning law; the field admits either vocabulary and the boundary decides which one this relation may use.
consumers.presenceLaw: REQUIRED exactly when satisfied is false; FORBIDDEN when satisfied is true; `satisfied` must be an actual boolean; and an explicit null is refused in BOTH branches, because a present key with a null value is not an absent key. Schema-enforced in repair.schema.json and decided again by workflows_model.admit_evidence_requirement, which routes every violation to CONFIG.INVALID - the class the owning schema validation and admit_atom already use for a malformed input - and adds no public detail code. The two boundaries are held EQUAL on an enumerated shape table, except for the cross-plane rows: this schema deliberately leaves the authoritative relation-registry lookup to admission. Its oneOf admits either outcome vocabulary on either relation; admission decides the plane from registry membership. JSON Schema can branch on const/enum under a broader string type, but this schema does not duplicate that registry as conditionals or fetch its rows. This is the selected division between schema validation and admission, not a limitation caused by the relation type.
consumers.authorityLimit: The field is a DISCLOSURE, not a grant and not a gate input. `applicable` is false whenever any requirement is unsatisfied, the evidence authority stays the sealed Run named by evidenceRunId, and apply requires a security authorization bound to the exact repairPlanId - which every edit to this value changes.

perRequirementConsumerBoundary.whyNotTheD9Vocabulary: The field previously named workflows common#/$defs/D9Deficiency, which cannot express four of the nine members its only producer emits: derivation-policy-unmet, external-consumers-unknown, input-closure-incomplete and resolution-incomplete have no member there. Only three readings were conforming and no document chose between them: write the D9-mapped value, which is `verdict-indeterminate` for ALL FOUR and therefore collapses exactly the per-row distinction this registry exists to keep - including resolution-incomplete, which section 4.6 step 6 mandates for a universal negative under unresolvedEdgePolicy=forbid over an affected target and which is the outcome a destructive unused-code repair recipe turns on; write the sufficiency value and be schema-invalid for four of nine; or omit the optional field and drop the disclosure. The repair is to retype the ONE per-requirement field, not to widen D9Deficiency: that enum is the whole-Run and comparison-step termination vocabulary of the inherited D9 exit contract, three of its members (convergence-exhausted, baseline-recipe-unsupported, query-completeness-unmet) name outcomes no per-requirement evaluation can produce, and widening it would change a D9 vocabulary to fix a workflows record. The DomainDetailCode route does not resolve it either: that registry carries a DIFFERENT five of the nine (budget-exhausted plus the four above), so the union of the two covers all nine and neither single field does.

The mirror is never allowed to be a superset: a workflows record must not be able to state a native outcome this unit does not define.
perRequirementConsumerBoundary.whatTheConsumerCarries: the SATISFACTION/DEFICIENCY PROJECTION of that result: `satisfied`, and exactly one DeficiencyV2 member when it is false, chosen by the section 10 precedence. `causes` and `disclosures` are NOT projected. They are the PRODUCER RESULT ARRAYS of that evaluation and are not fields of any record here: they are not members of CoverageResultV3, and some of them could not be - the confidence floor lives in RequirementV2, the external-consumer condition is requirement-relative, and `required-relation-missing` has no Coverage entry at all. What IS retained, and what a verifier re-derives, is the evidence the evaluation READ: the `coverage2` record with its own deficiency and nativeCause carrier per section 10, and the rest of the Run's committed closure. So the accurate statement is that the projection drops nothing that was retained, and that re-deriving the full result means re-running the evaluation over that retained evidence - not reading `causes` out of a stored field. No new wire field is introduced to carry them. The projection is total in the only sense a consumer needs: a failing requirement always has exactly one reported outcome, so omitting it is never lawful.
perRequirementConsumerBoundary.thisBlockOwnsTheNativePlaneOnly: Repair also admits a requirement over the two IMPORTED-EVIDENCE relations, `runtime-observation` and `history-change`. They mint no fact2, carry no sourceUniverse/targetUniverse and have no Coverage entry, so sufficiency_v2 has nothing to range over and would only report `required-relation-missing`, which says nothing true about an import. Their outcomes are owned by workflows/schemas/imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law and carry a DISJOINT vocabulary. An earlier revision described sufficiency_v2 as the only defined producer of that consumer field; that was false for those two relations and is corrected here. Which plane applies is decided at ADMISSION from relation-registry membership, never from the value.

value.standing: Normative and CLOSED. THE authority for TypeScriptConfigGraphV1 node `kind`. The schema enum publishes the three admissible values; this law publishes which one each node's path takes, which the prose previously delegated to `the schema and native admission` while neither stated it. It adds no enum member, no field and no record.
value.appliesTo: EVERY node of the retained graph - the selected entry AND every non-entry node reached through `extendsResolved`. There is no entry-only rule and no default for the rest. A non-entry node's kind affects no derived value (see derivedValueScope), which is exactly WHY it needed a published rule: nothing else pins it and it is still committed to the identity.
value.rule: kind is a total function of `node.path` alone. Take the BASENAME - the final `/`-separated segment of the path - and compare it BYTE-EXACTLY against the closed table below. A match takes the table's value; anything else is `other`. Nothing else is consulted: not the file's content, not its position in the graph, not whether it is the entry, not the directory, and not any caller assertion.
value.comparison: EXACT and case-SENSITIVE over the whole basename, on the UTF-8 bytes of the CanonicalPath as retained. No prefix, suffix, glob or stem matching; no case folding; no Unicode normalization beyond what CanonicalPath already requires; no extension-only test. `TSConfig.json`, `.tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.jsonc` are each `other`, and a host that lowercases the basename on a case-insensitive filesystem before comparing has produced a different graph and a different identity.

examples.note: a jsconfig entry stays a jsconfig program even when its bases are not
NON-ENTRY, reached as a base: the basename decides, the depth does not
THE DISCRIMINATING CASE. The widespread tsconfig*.json convention is NOT the rule here; see whyExactAndNotThePrefixConvention
same, as a shared base of the entry
case variant: the comparison is case-sensitive
an explicitly selected custom-named TypeScript configuration; its ENTRY kind is other and it still derives configOrigin tsconfig

value.derivedValueScope: `configOrigin` is derived from the SELECTED ENTRY node's kind only: `jsconfig` for a jsconfig entry, otherwise `tsconfig`, and `synthesized` exactly when there is no entry. So `other` and `tsconfig` both derive `tsconfig` at the entry, and a non-entry node's kind derives nothing at all. That is the whole reason this law is owed: `configOrigin` does NOT pin `kind`, so without a published rule two conforming hosts could disagree on a value that no derived field would ever contradict.
value.identityConsequence: kind sits INSIDE the hashed record. `tsconfigGraphHash` is the raw SHA-256 of C(TypeScriptConfigGraphV1); TypeScriptUniverseV2ResolvedInputs REQUIRES it and the binding checks equality; the universe H identity is fact.sourceUniverse and subject-scope.sourceUniverse, hence fact2, scope2, coverage2, view2, evidence3, seal3 and run3. Native owner admission re-runs this over retained payloads at identity-model.v3.open_run_closure; complete replay is identity-model.v3.close_run. Two readings of one repository containing `tsconfig.build.json` would therefore mint two RunIds and defeat independent replay across machines - the same defect class the analysis-spec `capabilityId` vocabulary was closed for, and closed the same way: by naming the authority beside the field. The historical evaluator2 graph reached evidence2/seal2/run2; that is the historical counterexample, not a current qualified claim.
value.whyExactAndNotThePrefixConvention: Both readings are natural and they disagree on real files, so one had to be chosen and written down. Exact basenames are chosen because `kind` records WHICH RECOGNIZED CONFIGURATION FILE this node is, not what a project chose to name a base; because the exact table is TOTAL, decidable from the retained path alone and identical on every filesystem, whereas a prefix rule would additionally have to decide `jsconfig.build.json`, an extensionless `tsconfig` and `tsconfig.jsonc`; and because it is the rule the selected model already derives, so publishing it changes no existing value. `other` is not a defect classification: it is the honest statement that this node's basename is neither recognized name, which is exactly what an explicitly selected custom-named configuration presents. NOTE ON SCOPE: this rationale is internal to this design. No claim is made here about what any external toolchain recognizes or what meaning it assigns to a filename convention; such a claim would be unverified from these bytes and is not needed to fix the reading.
value.notARecognitionRule: This law decides the `kind` of a node ALREADY IN the retained graph. Which config file is SELECTED as the entry, and which markers make a workspace unit at all, are section 1.4 U-1 and the shared discovery rule; nothing here mints a node, a unit or a program.
value.enforcedAt: native_evidence_model.typescript_config_graph_faults, which READS this table rather than restating it and reports `native.config-graph-kind-contradicts-path:<path>` for any node whose declared kind is not the derived one - so a relabelled entry, a relabelled base and an asserted `tsconfig` on `tsconfig.build.json` all refuse. ORDERING, precisely: typescript_universe_retained_input_faults computes the candidate C(record) digest and compares it to the universe's tsconfigGraphHash BEFORE it calls the graph faults, and both contribute to one fault list. So a candidate hash may well be computed; what never happens is ADMISSION - the universe is not admitted and no identity is accepted while any fault stands. The earlier wording `refuse before the graph digest is used` described the wrong boundary.
value.driftScope: The MODEL and this table cannot drift, because the model reads this table rather than restating it, and a control holds the derived values against it. Agreement between this table and the PROSE in native-evidence.md section 2.2 is NOT established by that control and is not claimed here: prose agreement is a review obligation, and asserting it by substring search would be a format-sensitive test rather than evidence.

value.standing: Normative and CLOSED. The PUBLIC TERMINATION each internal decision key of the capability and Coverage-cause guards derives to. An earlier revision published prose placeholders here - `request detail ...`, `operational record` - as if they were public detail codes; 14 of 16 branch targets refused the real DomainDetail schema and none of the keys was in internalAliases. Prose is not an enum value, and the claim that those targets were already members was false. Every value below is either a member of the closed workflows common D9 vocabularies, a member of the closed public DomainDetailCode registry, or an explicit declaration that the optional DomainDetail is ABSENT with the real operational carrier named.
value.carrier: The public carrier is workflows/schemas/common.schema.json#/$defs/StepTermination, not a bare DomainDetail. It carries `class` plus `errorCode`/`faultCause`/`reasonCodes`, and `domainDetail` is OPTIONAL. Where no existing DomainDetailCode member names the condition, domainDetail is lawfully ABSENT - the errorCode already names it - and the internal key is retained in the operational diagnostic record. That is the existing event law, not a new allowance.
value.originatingBoundaryLaw: admission-and-qualification section 1 fixes the actor/layer split: `Invalid external input is an admission rejection with the existing carrier's D9 code; an invalid host-generated internal layer is a host invariant fault.` The inherited d9-exit-contract.v1.14 completes it: nonAnalysisDerivation rule 2 puts authored-config errors and failed preconditions in request-rejected, rule 5 puts HOST failures in operational-failed, and axes.domainCondition distinguishes `host-fault` from `precondition-failed`. So the same internal key derives a DIFFERENT class and code depending on where the bad value entered, and calling every retained or direct spec `host-generated` was wrong: a retained spec of known external origin is an external input, and only a host BUG minting its own invalid internal layer is a host fault.
value.helperDoesNotGuessOrigin: The pure admission helpers - admit_requested_capabilities, admit_release_capability_registry, deficiency_cause_faults - are passed rows and nothing about provenance, so they emit the internal decision key ALONE. public_termination_for(key, origin) is the derivation the HOST calls with the origin it already holds; it refuses an origin the key cannot have, so a caller cannot launder a configuration error into a host fault or the reverse.
value.hostInvariantSuccessor: SELECTED NORMATIVE D9 COMPOSITION, published here rather than deferred. It inherits docs/coop/artifacts/d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json UNCHANGED and adds exactly one thing: the faultCause `host-invariant`, mapped to the EXISTING error code SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE. What was unrepresentable was the host-INVARIANT subtype specifically - other host-fault causes such as host-io, ledger-corrupt and provider-protocol already existed and were always representable - because StepTermination requires operational-failed to carry BOTH an errorCode and a non-none faultCause, and no declared cause named a host invariant violation. Borrowing host-io for it would be a different remedy. PRECISION: codeMaps.rule's `total and injective` is a property of the DECLARED CAUSE DOMAIN - every declared cause has exactly one code - and does NOT require every errorCode to have a preimage, so an errorCode without a cause was not a violation of totality; the earlier claim that the maps were non-total was wrong. Existing classes, exit codes, reason codes and error codes are unchanged, but this IS a D9 vocabulary extension: faultCause grows by one member, and saying otherwise would be false. Schema, workflow mapper and this registry must agree, every inherited mapping and golden is preserved, and an unknown cause still refuses.

native.requested-capability-duplicate-ow.why: Two requestedCapabilities rows carry the same (capabilityId, languageMode, workspaceRoot). The tuple names one cell of work for one unit and `required` is its attribute. Distinct rows can disagree on requiredness, whose value decides whether a missing Coverage entry contributes indeterminate; if admitted, that contradiction would enter analysisSpecDigest and PlanId. Default construction can instead produce identical rows through a host invariant violation. Both cases violate the one-row-per-tuple law; the precise admission paths are stated below. This is a MALFORMED SELECTION RECORD, not an unsatisfiable request and not a cell without a promise, so it takes the SAME origin-dependent routing as the other malformed-spec keys rather than the origin-independent REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE route above: who supplied the bad record decides whether it is an authored-configuration error, a failed admission precondition on an externally supplied or retained spec, or a host bug minting its own invalid internal layer. WHICH ROWS REACH THIS KEY, stated exactly, because an earlier revision said `exact whole-item duplicates never reach here - uniqueItems and the canonical-set order law refuse them first` and that was true of only one of the two paths. On an EXPLICITLY SUPPLIED spec it holds: admit_analysis_spec runs validate_foundation before the vocabulary helper, so byte-identical rows refuse on uniqueItems and this key sees only DISTINCT rows disagreeing on `required`. On the DEFAULT-CONSTRUCTION path it does not: default_capability_selection guards its own freshly built rows BEFORE admit_analysis_spec - because the schema's answer there is a generic ValidationError restating the whole instance - and those rows all carry required=True, so the duplicate it catches IS byte-identical. That guard names THIS key rather than a bespoke one, so the host-generated route below is reachable from the call site it was written for instead of from nothing. Both paths report the same (capabilityId, languageMode, workspaceRoot) subject.

value.aliasMapIsContextFree: Only a key whose public DETAIL is the same for EVERY origin may appear in public-detail-registry internalAliases, because that map is context-free. Two keys qualify and are aliased there: native.requested-capability-mode-not-selected -> PROVIDER.NOT_SELECTED and native.release-capability-undeclared -> native.capability-unavailable. The origin-DEPENDENT keys deliberately are NOT in that map - a context-free alias cannot express `CONFIG.INVALID when configured, absent when the host produced it` - and the keys whose detail is absent need no alias because they never surface as a DomainDetailCode. An earlier revision claimed all 14 belonged there and that the edit was mechanical; both claims were wrong.
value.enforcedAt: native_evidence_model public_termination_for derives the termination and validates it against the real StepTermination schema; the guards themselves emit only the internal key.
value.possibleOriginsLaw: Every key declares the boundaries at which it CAN arise, and a derivation refuses any other. A release declaration is never a user's configuration and a configured capability is never the host's own authenticated release input, so a caller cannot launder one actor's fault into another's. An origin-INDEPENDENT key still has possible origins - what is independent is the resulting class and code, not who could have caused it.
value.unsupportedTypedIsNotOnThisTable: An UNSUPPORTED-TYPED request is admitted and ANSWERED, never refused: the Run closes and its Coverage carries `unknown` with the deficiency the OWNING DERIVATION selects under the section 10 precedence. For a relation the admitted universe cannot serve at all - a compiler-free references request under syntax-only - that is language-tier-unsupported with capability-missing, and it OUTRANKS provider-unavailable. A capability the release merely did not declare available carries provider-unavailable with capability-missing only where no more specific deficiency applies, and a CANDIDATE-ONLY capability has no Coverage entry at all - its public route is the advisory native.capability-unavailable notice in CommandEnvelope.availability, whose complete ownership tuple is defined in section 1.4. An earlier revision stated the provider-unavailable pair here as THE outcome for both cases, which contradicted the precedence and the candidate-only distinction section 1.4 publishes. Neither case may be converted into an admission refusal.
value.envelopeErrorsComposition: A kind=failure CommandEnvelope REQUIRES a nonempty `errors` array of DomainDetail, so `termination.domainDetail` being OPTIONAL does not complete the public failure surface: a route that lawfully leaves it absent still owes the envelope a detail. An earlier revision stopped at StepTermination admission, and a minimal failure envelope built from the externally-supplied and host-generated routes refused `errors is a required property`. failure_envelope_errors composes it: where the termination carries a detail the array is EXACTLY that detail, so the two surfaces can never disagree; where it does not, the route's own `envelopeDetail` supplies one. Every code used is a member of the closed public DomainDetailCode registry. Four members were ADDED there rather than borrowing an unrelated remedy - native.capability-spec-invalid, native.release-declaration-invalid, native.coverage-cause-unsupported and HOST.INVARIANT_VIOLATED - because `a supplied spec names an unregistered capability`, `the installed release declaration is malformed`, `the provider emitted an unsupported deficiency/cause pair` and `the host violated its own invariant` are four different things for a caller to do next. Reuse was taken wherever it was honest: external configuration keeps CONFIG.INVALID and a NOT-SELECTED cell keeps PROVIDER.NOT_SELECTED. Before a Plan or Run exists no run envelope is fabricated - the failure envelope carries the termination, its errors and the request id, and nothing else.
value.remedyKeyingConstraint: NORMATIVE MAINTENANCE CONSTRAINT on the remedy table, promoted here from a source comment so it is part of the published law rather than advice a reader may miss. PUBLIC_ROUTE_REMEDIES is keyed by PUBLIC CODE, not by internal key. Several keys route to one code - native.requested-capability-unregistered, native.requested-capability-mode-unregistered and native.requested-capability-duplicate-ownership-tuple all reach CONFIG.INVALID under external-configuration, and all three reach native.capability-spec-invalid as the externally-supplied-spec envelope detail - so ONE string must remain true for EVERY key that reaches that code, and a key whose remedy would be a DIFFERENT next step may not simply reuse the code. THIS IS CURRENTLY SATISFIED, not merely intended: the two strings widened for the ownership tuple state both the unregistered-name condition and the one-row-per-tuple condition, and the default-construction path added later routes to the same key and is covered by the same two sentences plus HOST.INVARIANT_VIOLATED, which is true of a host emitting two rows for one cell. The structural alternative - keying the remedy by (code, internal key) - is deliberately NOT taken: it changes the shape of an existing table for a case honest sentences already cover, and no key in this composition needs it. What is owed instead is exact: adding a key that routes to an existing code obliges its author to check that code's remedy is a true next step for the new condition and to widen it or choose another code if it is not.
value.subjectNormalization: The guards emit COLON-SUFFIXED refusal strings - native.requested-capability-unregistered:made-up-capability, native.coverage-cause-not-for-deficiency:input-closure-incomplete:capability-missing - so a normalizer matching the whole string would find no registered key. normalize_internal_key matches the LONGEST registered key followed by a colon and takes the remainder as the subject, which is what reaches DomainDetail.subject so a caller sees WHICH value was refused. A raw string matching no registered key REFUSES (native.public-route-key-unregistered) rather than passing through, as the public registry aliasRule requires of an unknown key; an origin a key cannot have refuses too (native.public-route-origin-not-possible).
value.subjectBoundLaw: DomainDetail.subject is BoundedText (1024) while a refused VALUE can be far longer: a structurally valid languageMode may be 4096 characters, and the composed subject then reached 4149 and made the whole failure envelope schema-invalid at termination.domainDetail.subject or errors[0].subject. bounded_subject elides: the registered KEY is preserved verbatim - it selects the code, the class and the origin - and only the offending value is elided, keeping a leading window plus the SHA-256 of the untruncated subject's UTF-8 bytes. UNITS, because the two operations differ: `raw` is the composed subject as an admitted UNICODE SCALAR STRING, and length and slicing count UNICODE CODE POINTS - what BoundedText's JSON Schema maxLength counts - not UTF-8 bytes and not UTF-16 code units; the SHA-256 input is exactly raw encoded as UTF-8 with NO additional normalization, rendered as 64 lowercase hex characters after the ASCII marker `...#sha256:`, giving exactly 1024 code points. A non-ASCII value can therefore have a UTF-8 byte length above 1024 while its scalar length does not, and the two must not be conflated. GUARANTEE: distinct long values are distinguished under the ORDINARY COLLISION-RESISTANCE ASSUMPTION for SHA-256, not by any impossibility claim, and the guarantee is confined to what is PUBLISHED - the bounded subject and its digest. No separate retained store of the untruncated value is promised or named here; a host keeping its own operational log matches it by recomputing this digest. Emitting the untruncated string would be schema-invalid, dropping the subject would lose attribution, and reclassifying the input error as success would be false; the code, class and origin are never changed by the elision.

value.standing: Normative and CLOSED. The per-language capability mapping of the bundled grammar set, published here so a consumer can reconstruct it without reading author code. syntaxClass is NOT caller-selected: a grammar row declaring a class other than the one this registry assigns to its languageId is refused at grammar-bundle admission, in both directions.
value.source: native_evidence_model.v2.BUNDLED_GRAMMARS (the same table the shared discovery rule uses for the grammar-only membership path) and native-evidence section 6.3.

classLaw.code: The language has the section 6.3 body spans - function, method, closure/lambda, impl item and block bodies - and a published L2/L3 normalisation table. Bears clone body identity (clones@normalized-body-hash) and the code-construct syntax relations (declares/literal/control-flow @ syntactic). Its languageId MUST be a member of foundation body-language-version.languageId, because that identifier enters the clone preimage.
classLaw.data-document: A bundled grammar for a data or document format. It has no section 6.3 body spans, and this kit publishes no tokenisation, literalKind mapping or normalisation law for it. Its files are grammar-only MEMBERS - accounted, inventoried, never unsupported-file - bearing file/package/vcs-change inventory evidence under the syntax universe. It mints NO body identity, no suffix of it appears in the syntax dialect table, and its languageId MUST NOT be in body-language-version.languageId. A clone or code-construct request against it is explicitly UNAVAILABLE (language-tier-unsupported for that capability), never a complete empty clone result, which would read as a finding of no clones.

value.unbundledLanguages: A language with no bundled grammar is not representable here at all: its files are unsupported-file with reason no-bundled-grammar, and its languageId is outside the SyntaxGrammarBundleV1 vocabulary. Adding one is a deliberate registry change, not a caller choice.
value.futureCapability: Data-format syntax facts (for example literal@syntactic over JSON or YAML) would require a published tokenisation and literalKind law. None exists in this kit, so the mapping above does not promise them. This is a bounded future capability, deliberately not invented here.
value.enforcementBoundaries: This registry is the authority at THREE boundaries, not one. (1) Grammar-bundle admission: a row's declared syntaxClass must equal the registered one, in both directions. (2) Every admitted fact2 under a syntax universe: every ANCHOR PATH must be read by a SELECTED grammar whose capability set contains that relation@rung. (3) Every requested subject-scope under a syntax universe, INCLUDING an empty view: judged on the committed examined extent, where a code capability needs at least one extent path read by a selected code grammar, and a capability no selected grammar bears is unavailable. INVENTORY CAPABILITIES (file@enumerated, package@manifest-declared, vcs-change@vcs-reported) are ALWAYS available and are never grammar-gated at boundary (2) OR boundary (3). An earlier revision stated that exemption only inside boundary (3), and boundary (2) read as an unconditional every-anchor rule; a literal implementer therefore refused the very inventory facts boundary (3) had just promised were unconditionally available, which made an inventoried .py path inventoriable and unrepresentable at the same time. The exemption belongs to both because it is a property of the RELATION, not of the boundary: an inventory fact is not read by a grammar at all - it is the snapshot inventory row, the manifest declaration or the VCS observation - so there is no grammar for it to be gated on. Independently of this exemption the relation registry anchorLaw closes the inventory class at ZERO anchors, so an inventory fact names no anchor path for boundary (2) to test in the first place; the two laws agree and neither depends on the other. An earlier revision enforced only (1), which constrains what a bundle says about itself and not what a Run claims: Markdown declares facts, complete empty declares/clones Coverage and references@resolved-binding under resolutionAttempted=false all admitted. None of the three consults a claimed coverage value, a caller-declared class, or whether facts exist.
value.unavailableRequestDisclosure: A well-formed request for a capability this universe cannot serve is DISCLOSED, not answered and not refused outright: coverage `unknown`, deficiency `language-tier-unsupported`, nativeCause `capability-missing` - existing vocabulary, mapped in native-evidence section 10. A false `complete`, a wrong or null cause and a wrong deficiency each refuse with their own typed reason. The capability is retained: a data-grammar inventory Run and a code-grammar declares/clones Run still close with a genuine complete and no deficiency.
value.selectionMatters: An UNSELECTED grammar lends no capability. Selection is committed in the universe identity, so a bundle that ships a grammar the universe did not select cannot make its capabilities available.
value.inventoryIsNotGrammarGated: Normative. A snapshot inventories every file it contains, including ones no bundled grammar reads, so requiring a grammar per inventory row would silently narrow the promise this registry makes. The three inventory capabilities are therefore exempt at every boundary this registry owns, on every path - unsupported suffix, extensionless, data-document and code alike - and a `vcs-change` on a `deleted` path that is not in the snapshot at all. This is an exemption from GRAMMAR OWNERSHIP only. It does not exempt an inventory fact from its relation's snapshot joins (path in the inventory; for `file` also the content digest, the byte length and custody of the retained bytes), from own-scope attribution, or from the anchorLaw; and it does not make a CODE fact admissible merely because some other anchor of the same Run is on a supported path.
